brief: Citi raised its 12-month crypto price targets: Bitcoin's base case moves from $82,000 to $113,000 (bull $151,000, bear $43,000), Ether's from $2,240 to $3,028 (bull $4,244, bear $1,157), on activity, macro backdrop and ETF flows. The breakout followed a Treasury buyback announcement (debasement fears) and an administration meeting with crypto industry insiders the same day (regulatory news), with the exact cause hard to isolate; Citi's Alex Saunders infers regulatory news mattered at least as much, since Bitcoin's reaction to the buyback was delayed relative to gold and bonds. BTC and ETH trade above their 200-day moving averages, ETF holders are closer to profit, and inflows have resumed; Citi raised its base-case flow assumption from flat and kept a 20% user-growth adoption assumption, estimating $1bn of BTC ETF flow moves price 3.5%. ETH's estimate rose more on picked-up user activity, reflecting its programmable-money use case versus Bitcoin's store-of-value framing. Separately, the Senate's Clarity Act stalled, but SEC rule announcements eased negative sentiment ('a temporary but meaningful positive'); Citi flags 2028 administration-change rollback risk as outside its forecast horizon.
